London pigeon tour

On our London Pigeon Tour, meet the pigeons of Trafalgar Square and St. James’s Park!

Your guide will bring you around the historic London park — the site of the royal aviary of King James I — and share the fascinating story of London pigeons. Pigeons have served as wartime messengers, aristocratic status symbols, beloved fancy breeds (Charles Darwin bred pigeons!), and so much more.

You’ll visit nearby flocks and observe pigeons coexisting with the famous park waterbirds, defying anti-pigeon spikes and netting, and interacting with everyday Londoners, as they have for thousands of years.

Book your tour

5 stars on TripAdvisor!

What you’ll do

  • We’ll start the tour in Trafalgar Square and learn a little bit about the history of pigeons in London
  • On our way to St. James’s Park, we’ll learn how to spot and identify anti-pigeon architecture
  • We will visit multiple pigeon flocks in the park and have a chance to observe their behavior. We’ll learn about how they reproduce, navigate, and adapt to urban life
  • We’ll meet other types of birds, from the famous park pelicans to grey herons, parakeets (fellow ferals!), greylag geese, coots, and many more, and learn how they fit into the history of the park
  • The tour ends outside of St. James’s Café, where we’ll talk about the complicated pigeon/human relationship and their role as pests, pets, posties, and beyond.

What to expect

Duration

This tour lasts 90 mins - 2 hrs.

Out of respect for your time, we aim to start the tour right on time. Please plan to arrive a few minutes early.

Most tours end around 90 minutes, but sometimes run a little longer based on the interests of the group. We recommend planning for 2 hours.

Distance

About 1.5 miles (2.4 km)

There are few places to sit along the way.

Meetup location

We’ll meet in Trafalgar Square. The tour will conclude outside of St. James’s Cafè, about a 10 minute walk from Trafalgar Square.

Accessibility

The pavement in the park is relatively flat. We are not aware of permanent obstacles to wheelchairs or other mobility devices along our route. Unexpected obstacles (like construction) may occur, but we’ll route around them.

Generally, we will be walking and standing, but there are occasional benches available along the route.

The toilets at Marlborough Gate and in Trafalgar Square are accessible.

If you have specific mobility needs or questions, please get in touch, and we’ll work with you to meet your needs.

Toilets

There are public toilets available at the meetup point. There are also toilets at St. James’s Café (although you may need to make a purchase to access them) and public toilets by Marlborough Gate and the Horse Guard Parade Café.

The charge for public toilets is 20p and you will need to pay via card/contactless.

Food and water

Aside from the park cafes (St. James’s, Horse Guard Parade, and Storey’s Gate), there are refreshments kiosks throughout the park, including at Marlborough Gate, Horse Shoe Bend, Artillery Memorial, and the playground.

There is a drinking fountain near Marlborough Gate. Just inside the gate, facing towards the park, turn down the left-hand path. The fountain will be on your left.

Public transportation

By Tube: Charing Cross (Bakerloo and Northern lines) is the nearest Tube station, with an entrance/exit on Trafalgar Square.

By bus: There are numerous bus routes that serve Trafalgar Square. You can plan your journey using the Transport for London bus map.

By train: The Charing Cross railway station (Southeastern Railway) is about a three minute walk from Trafalgar Square.

What to bring

Pigeon tours are rain-or-shine — just like pigeons — so make sure to be prepared.

  • Weather-appropriate clothes and footwear
  • Sun protection, including sunscreen, sunglasses, maybe a hat.
  • Water
  • Cash (or Venmo) if you’d like to tip your guide
  • Your binoculars, if you have a pair you like
